planting.note: Plant tuber sections 3-4 inches deep around the last frost date in well-drained soil in full sun; Clearwater was discovered in Maine and is prized for tubers that stay smooth and round rather than knobby, making them far quicker to clean than most sunchoke stock.

directions: Plant tuber sections 3-4 inches deep in well-drained soil around the last frost date. Clearwater is a Maine-origin Jerusalem artichoke selection valued among sunchoke growers for two traits that set it apart from most named varieties: tubers that form smooth, rounded, potato-like shapes rather than the knobby, eye-covered lumps typical of the species, and a notably mild, sweet, nutty flavor that lacks the faint piney or resinous aftertaste some people notice in standard sunchoke stock. Plants are tall even by Jerusalem artichoke standards, often topping 11-12 feet by late summer, and are crowned with the same small yellow sunflower blooms typical of the species, which are also edible. Clearwater spreads by underground tubers less aggressively than many sunchoke varieties, producing fewer long runners, though it should still be given a dedicated bed since any missed tuber will resprout. Dig tubers after fall frost kills the foliage and continue harvesting through winter into early spring; cold exposure sweetens the flavor further by converting stored inulin to sugar.
